what_its_for: Famciclovir is an antiviral medicine used to treat infections caused by certain viruses. It is commonly used to treat cold sores (fever blisters), genital herpes, and shingles (a painful rash caused by the chickenpox virus). It does not cure these infections, but it helps sores heal faster, reduces pain, and can lower the chance of the infection spreading to others.
how_to_take: Take famciclovir by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep a steady amount of the medicine in your body. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: Your dose will depend on what condition is being treated, how serious it is, and how well your kidneys work. Common doses include: For cold sores - 1500 mg as a single dose taken at the first sign of a sore. For genital herpes outbreaks - 1000 mg twice in one day, or 125 mg twice a day for 5 days, depending on your doctor's instructions. For shingles - 500 mg three times a day for 7 days. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Since this medicine works best when started early, try not to miss doses.
storage: Store famciclovir tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid sexual contact when you have sores or blisters present, because famciclovir does not completely stop the spread of herpes to a partner. Always use a condom during sexual activity to reduce the risk of spreading the virus. Avoid touching sores and then touching your eyes or other body parts. Wash your hands often. Let your doctor know before taking other medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as some may interact with famciclovir.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: confusion, agitation, or unusual changes in your mood or behavior; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination, swelling in your legs or feet; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, itching, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing; severe dizziness or feeling faint; or if your symptoms do not improve or get worse. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
when_it_works: Famciclovir works best when started as soon as possible after your symptoms begin, ideally within the first 6 to 48 hours depending on the condition being treated. For cold sores and genital herpes, it works fastest when taken at the very first sign of a tingling, itching, or burning feeling. Most people notice improvement within 2 to 4 days. Shingles pain and rash usually improve within about a week of starting treatment.
special_populations: Older adults and people with kidney disease may need a lower dose because their kidneys may not remove the medicine from the body as quickly. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on how well your kidneys are working. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before taking this medicine, as its safety in pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully studied. This medicine is generally not used in children, so talk to your doctor if it is being considered for a child.
